top_module.name: motor_control_top
top_module.description: Top-level control-plane and transport-plane wrapper for an external runtime. It exposes a 64-bit software register window, bounded request/response streaming interfaces, a compact actuator command interface, and fault/busy/fallback status outputs. It contains the safety FSM, request assembler, response validator, watchdog/timeout logic, clamp and optional slew limiting, abort handling, sticky fault management, and safe-fallback behavior.
top_module.functionality: Implements software-programmable control/status registers including enable, start_request, abort, clear_fault, model_id, request_seq, expected_response_seq, max_response_age, timeout_cycles, clamp_min, clamp_max, safe_fallback_cmd, request_flags, optional slew-limit parameters, and readback status. On enabled start_request, it assembles a compact 128-bit request frame containing only metadata and scalar descriptors for an external runtime, asserts tx_valid until tx_ready, and marks the request issued only upon handshake. It tracks outstanding request state, response age, and timeout deadlines. On valid inbound response, it verifies expected sequence, response type, and integrity bits/CRC/parity if implemented, rejects stale/duplicate/malformed/mismatched responses, and forces safe fallback on rejection. Approved responses can update the actuator command, which is then clamped to clamp_min..clamp_max and, if enabled, slew-limited. The module exposes busy_out while awaiting transaction completion or actuator acceptance, and fallback_out whenever safe fallback is active due to timeout, invalid response, software disable, abort, or safety fault. The fault latch is sticky and clearable only via dedicated software clear_fault when no outstanding transaction remains or after explicit abort.
responsibilities: Own the top-level software register window and register readback semantics.
Own the request framing and tx_valid/tx_ready handshake behavior.
Own the response qualification, sequence validation, age checking, and timeout logic.
Own the safety FSM across IDLE, ISSUE_REQUEST, WAIT_RESPONSE, VALIDATE_RESPONSE, APPLY_COMMAND, FALLBACK, and ABORT states.
Own actuator command clamping and optional bounded slew limiting.
Own sticky fault, busy, and fallback status generation.
Preserve single-outstanding ordering and safe default behavior on reset and fault.
top_module.reset_behavior: On reset, all control registers, counters, state bits, handshake qualifiers, and command outputs initialize to safe values. tx_valid deasserts, rx_ready deasserts unless a response window is armed, act_valid deasserts, act_cmd returns to safe_fallback_cmd if programmed or zero otherwise, busy_out deasserts, fallback_out asserts only if dictated by a post-reset safety policy after programming (default inactive), and fault_out clears to zero. Any pending transaction is cancelled and no stale response may be accepted after reset release until a new start_request is issued.
behavior_rules: cfg_ready shall indicate accepted register accesses or always-ready behavior as long as the access decodes to a valid location; invalid addresses return defined status and do not perturb safety state.

Software-visible registers shall include at minimum enable, start_request, abort, clear_fault, model_id, request_seq, expected_response_seq, max_response_age, timeout_cycles, clamp_min, clamp_max, safe_fallback_cmd, request_flags, and readback status bits.
start_request is edge/level qualified by enable and shall launch only when no outstanding transaction is active.
The request frame on tx_data shall be compact and bounded, containing only metadata and scalar descriptors; it shall not expose raw geometry payloads or any tensor/field arrays.
tx_valid remains asserted until tx_ready is observed; the request is considered issued only on that handshake.
rx_ready shall assert only while a response is expected and the block is able to capture the response safely.
Responses are accepted only when sequence, type, and integrity checks pass, and only for the currently outstanding request.
Stale, duplicate, malformed, unexpected, or sequence-mismatched responses shall be rejected, set a sticky fault bit, and force safe fallback.
Timeout comparison shall use timeout_cycles or max_response_age, whichever is architecturally selected as the active deadline basis, but never both in a conflicting way.
act_cmd shall always be clamped to clamp_min..clamp_max before being presented to the actuator interface.
busy_out shall remain asserted while a request is outstanding, while awaiting response validation, or while waiting for actuator acceptance if act_valid is held high.
fallback_out shall assert whenever the safe fallback command is active due to timeout, invalid response, software disable, abort, or safety fault.
fault latch clearing requires a dedicated clear_fault write and shall be blocked while a live transaction remains unless an explicit abort has completed.
A software abort cancels pending requests, deasserts tx_valid, returns the FSM to idle, and enters safe fallback.
All comparisons, counters, and state transitions shall be implemented using standard-cell synthesizable logic only.

modules.name: motor_control_register_map
modules.description: Register file and decode submodule for software control/status access. It translates the 64-bit memory-mapped window into semantic control fields and status readbacks used by the top-level safety and transport logic.
modules.functionality: Implements a compact software-visible register map. It captures programmed control fields, provides decoded semantic outputs to the safety FSM and transport adapter, and returns status readbacks including busy/fault/fallback state, outstanding state, last accepted sequence, last command, and error code. It must not infer any bulk payload storage or expose raw geometry data.
responsibilities: Decode cfg_addr/cfg_we/cfg_re accesses into stable control registers.
Latch enable/start_request/abort/clear_fault and programmable scalar descriptors.
Provide readback of current configuration and safety/status fields.
Hold reset-safe defaults and expose deterministic read data for unmapped locations if required by architecture.
Present semantic outputs to top-level control logic without hidden derivation from the transport bus.
modules.reset_behavior: All registers clear to safe values on reset. enable deasserts, start_request deasserts, abort deasserts, clear_fault deasserts, programmable limits and commands default to zero unless architecture chooses a safe fallback default, and cfg_rdata returns a defined safe value. No request may be launched during reset.
behavior_rules: Semantic control outputs are stable registered values suitable for direct use by the top-level FSM.
Status fields are read-only from the perspective of software and are sourced from the top-level control/safety block.
Any write to clear_fault shall be visible as a one-cycle pulse or level-qualified control according to the top-level architecture, but must be explicit and synthesizable.
The register map shall not contain payload memories, FIFOs, or bulk history banks.
Software disable must be representable as cfg_enable deassertion and shall force safe fallback through the top-level FSM.

modules.name: motor_control_transport_adapter
modules.description: Bounded transport-plane framing and capture adapter for the external runtime service. It assembles outbound request frames, tracks a single outstanding request, captures inbound response frames, and exposes compact metadata for validation and command derivation.
modules.functionality: Builds the compact outbound request packet and manages the single outstanding request lifecycle. It exposes request issuance status, age/deadline tracking, and a compact response summary extracted from the 128-bit inbound packet for downstream validation. It must never expand into bulk payload handling or unbounded buffering.
responsibilities: Assemble tx_data from model ID, sequence, request type/flags, and scalar descriptors.
Assert tx_valid until tx_ready handshake completes.
Track outstanding request and sequence association.
Compute age/deadline status using cfg_timeout_cycles and/or cfg_max_response_age as designed.
Capture rx_data only when rx_valid and rx_ready are both asserted.
Extract compact response metadata for validation and command generation.
Support abort by canceling outstanding request context and returning to idle.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, no request is outstanding, request age is zero, tx_valid deasserts, rx_ready deasserts or remains safely gated until a request is pending, response summary outputs clear to safe values, and any latent issuance state is discarded.
behavior_rules: A request can be launched only when enabled and no other request is outstanding.
tx_valid must remain asserted until handshake completion.
rx_ready must only assert when a response is expected and the adapter can safely capture it.
Only one outstanding request is supported; later architecture changes for multiple outstanding requests would require a compact sequence scoreboard, but that is not part of this contract.
The adapter shall not retain arbitrary history or raw geometry payloads.
Any abort or timeout shall clear outstanding state and prevent stale response acceptance.

modules.name: motor_control_response_validator
modules.description: Validation submodule that checks response sequence, response type, age, and integrity metadata. It converts transport metadata into a compact approval or rejection decision used by the safety FSM.
modules.functionality: Performs strict response qualification. It accepts only responses that match the active request sequence, have an expected response type, pass integrity checks, and arrive before the deadline. All stale, duplicate, malformed, or sequence-mismatched responses are rejected and converted into a sticky fault indication upstream.
responsibilities: Compare response sequence against request sequence and configured expectation.
Check response type and compact integrity metadata.
Gate approval on age/deadline status.
Emit a rejection code for status reporting.
Pass through only approved response command metadata to the command limiter/actuator path.
Remain purely synthesizable and side-effect free except for registered outputs.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, no response is accepted, rejection_code clears to zero, and approved outputs default to safe values.
behavior_rules: A response is valid only when request_outstanding is asserted and the sequence matches the expected active sequence.
Any integrity failure, type mismatch, deadline expiration, or age violation shall reject the response.
Rejected responses must contribute to a sticky fault condition in the top-level safety FSM.
The module shall not perform any floating-point or geometry processing; it only handles metadata-level validation.
Approved responses must not bypass the clamp or safety state machine.

modules.name: motor_control_command_limiter
modules.description: Command post-processing block that clamps approved actuator commands to configured bounds and optionally applies a bounded slew limit before the command is presented to the actuator interface.
modules.functionality: Derives the final actuator command from approved response metadata or the programmed safe fallback command. It clamps the command to clamp_min..clamp_max and, if enabled, bounds the step between updates by cfg_slew_limit_step. It also arbitrates act_valid/act_ready acceptance.
responsibilities: Select between approved command and safe fallback command.
Clamp to programmable min/max limits.
Optionally apply bounded slew limiting.
Assert act_valid when a new command is available for the actuator interface.
Hold act_valid until act_ready is observed, if required by implementation.
Provide registered limited and clamped command observability for status reporting.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, act_valid deasserts, act_cmd defaults to safe_fallback_cmd if available or zero otherwise, limited_cmd and clamped_cmd clear to safe values, and no command is marked applied until the interface accepts it.
behavior_rules: The final actuator command shall never exceed clamp_min..clamp_max.
If slew limiting is enabled, delta to the previous command shall be bounded by cfg_slew_limit_step.
If safe fallback is active, the output command shall be derived from safe_fallback_cmd and then clamped.
act_valid shall remain asserted until act_ready acknowledges the command when the architecture requires handshake retention.
The block shall not source any command from raw geometry or unvalidated data.

modules.name: motor_control_safety_fsm
modules.description: Safety and sequencing FSM that coordinates register decode, request issuance, response validation, command release, timeout handling, sticky fault management, software disable, and abort behavior.
modules.functionality: Implements the mandated clear FSM behavior and safety policy. It gates request launch on enable, tracks outstanding transaction state, reacts to timeout/rejection/abort, latches faults, and holds fallback outputs until software clears the fault under allowed conditions. It also provides status readbacks for the register map.
responsibilities: Coordinate IDLE, ISSUE_REQUEST, WAIT_RESPONSE, VALIDATE_RESPONSE, APPLY_COMMAND, FALLBACK, and ABORT states.
Generate busy_out and fallback_out based on live transaction and safety state.
Latch and clear faults according to software policy.
Enforce enable/start_request/abort semantics.
Sequence and age validation must occur before command release.
Expose status readbacks for last error, last accepted sequence, and last actuator command.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, the FSM returns to IDLE, all one-hot state outputs clear except IDLE, fault_latched clears, busy_out deasserts, fallback_out is safe-inactive unless policy dictates safe fallback as the default command state, and status readbacks clear to known values.
behavior_rules: Only one state may be active in a one-hot or equivalent encoding at a time.
A request may only issue when enabled and no fault or abort condition blocks it.
Timeout, invalid response, stale response, software disable, or abort shall transition to fallback or abort as appropriate.
fault_latched may be cleared only by cfg_clear_fault when no outstanding transaction remains or after explicit abort completion.
busy_out shall remain high while a request is outstanding or while awaiting actuator acceptance.
fallback_out shall assert whenever the safe fallback command is active due to safety policy.
The FSM shall not drive any unbounded or analog behavior.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_enable
inter_module_signals.description: Software enable control distributed from the register map to transport and safety control.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_start_request
inter_module_signals.description: Software start request pulse or level distributed to request issuance and safety sequencing.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_abort
inter_module_signals.description: Software abort control distributed to cancel pending requests and force safe fallback.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_clear_fault
inter_module_signals.description: Software clear-fault control distributed to the safety FSM.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_model_id
inter_module_signals.description: Model identifier used when assembling the outbound request frame.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_request_seq
inter_module_signals.description: Requested sequence number for the outbound request frame.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_expected_response_seq
inter_module_signals.description: Expected response sequence number used by transport capture and validation.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_max_response_age
inter_module_signals.description: Maximum response age threshold for transport-side deadline tracking.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_timeout_cycles
inter_module_signals.description: Programmable timeout threshold distributed to transport and safety logic.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_clamp_min
inter_module_signals.description: Minimum clamp bound for actuator command limiting.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_clamp_max
inter_module_signals.description: Maximum clamp bound for actuator command limiting.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_safe_fallback_cmd
inter_module_signals.description: Safe fallback actuator command programmed by software.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_request_flags
inter_module_signals.description: Request flags and optional integrity/behavior metadata for outbound frame assembly.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_slew_limit_en
inter_module_signals.description: Enable for optional actuator slew limiting.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_slew_limit_step
inter_module_signals.description: Maximum commanded step size when slew limiting is enabled.

inter_module_signals.name: request_outstanding
inter_module_signals.description: Single-outstanding transaction status propagated to validation, status readback, and safety FSM.

inter_module_signals.name: request_issued
inter_module_signals.description: Indicates the outbound request handshake completed.

inter_module_signals.name: request_seq_active
inter_module_signals.description: Active request sequence number used for response matching.

inter_module_signals.name: deadline_expired
inter_module_signals.description: Timeout indication used by validation and safety policy.

inter_module_signals.name: request_age
inter_module_signals.description: Request age is observed for debug/status purposes; actual status encoding is handled by the register map and safety FSM contract.

inter_module_signals.name: response_valid
inter_module_signals.description: Captured inbound response validity handed to the response validator.

inter_module_signals.name: response_seq
inter_module_signals.description: Captured response sequence handed to the response validator.

inter_module_signals.name: response_type
inter_module_signals.description: Captured response type metadata handed to the response validator.

inter_module_signals.name: response_integrity_ok
inter_module_signals.description: Compact integrity indication from the transport adapter handed to the response validator.

inter_module_signals.name: response_cmd_raw
inter_module_signals.description: Raw compact response command recommendation handed to the validator and then to the command limiter if approved.

inter_module_signals.name: response_status
inter_module_signals.description: Compact response status metadata handed to the response validator.

inter_module_signals.name: response_age_ok
inter_module_signals.description: Age qualification from transport capture handed to the response validator.

inter_module_signals.name: response_accepted
inter_module_signals.description: Approved response indication distributed to command generation, safety FSM, and status readback.

inter_module_signals.name: response_rejected
inter_module_signals.description: Rejected response indication delivered to the safety FSM to latch fault and force fallback.

inter_module_signals.name: rejection_code
inter_module_signals.description: Compact rejection reason propagated for status reporting.

inter_module_signals.name: approved_cmd_raw
inter_module_signals.description: Approved raw command recommendation that enters the limiter stage.

inter_module_signals.name: approved_status
inter_module_signals.description: Approved status metadata passed to the command limiter.

inter_module_signals.name: approved_seq_match
inter_module_signals.description: Sequence match indication used for status traceability.

inter_module_signals.name: use_fallback
inter_module_signals.description: Fallback policy signal selecting safe-fallback command generation.

inter_module_signals.name: act_cmd
inter_module_signals.description: Final clamped actuator command propagated to status readback and safety tracking.

inter_module_signals.name: fallback_cmd_active
inter_module_signals.description: Indicates the command limiter is currently sourcing the safe fallback command.

inter_module_signals.name: command_applied
inter_module_signals.description: Safety FSM acknowledgment that the command path has been accepted/applied.

inter_module_signals.name: fault_latched
inter_module_signals.description: Sticky fault indication used for status readback and top-level fault_out.

inter_module_signals.name: busy_out
inter_module_signals.description: Busy indication used for status readback and top-level busy_out.

inter_module_signals.name: fallback_out
inter_module_signals.description: Fallback indication used for status readback and top-level fallback_out.

inter_module_signals.name: status_last_error_code
inter_module_signals.description: Last error code propagated into software-readable status.

inter_module_signals.name: status_request_outstanding
inter_module_signals.description: Outstanding transaction status returned to the register map.

inter_module_signals.name: status_last_response_ok
inter_module_signals.description: Indicates whether the last response was accepted.

inter_module_signals.name: status_last_seq
inter_module_signals.description: Last accepted sequence number for software readback.

inter_module_signals.name: status_last_act_cmd
inter_module_signals.description: Last actuator command for software readback.
